subject: Regression with spatially autocorrelated random effects

messages.author: fa6f5d4c13c0cca5
messages.subject: Regression with spatially autocorrelated random effects
parts:
I'm trying to add a geostatistical component to a hierarchical regression with random intercepts.

y[i] ~ N(alpha[site[i]] + X[i]*beta, sigma)
alpha ~ MVN(mu, Sigma), Sigma = exp(-lambda * D)

Where alpha is a k dimensional vector, mu is a k-vector of 0's, D is a k by k distance matrix, and lambda is a positive parameter modelling the strength of the spatial autocorrelation.

The model keeps running into max treedepth errors; increasing the parameter up to 12 gives no improved response, and I'm still waiting for the runs with larger values to finish.  The model is also occasionally sampling lambda as 0, resulting in a Sigma of all 1's, causing a rejected Metropolis step; I'm unsure what prior would work best to avoid this. 

I've tried using the multivariate Matt trick, but I'm not convinced I'm using it correctly.  I'm not particularly familiar with Cholesky decomposition, so I am wondering if I misspecified the model. 

Any assistance would be greatly appreciated

messages.author: 4e90fa9f1b035969
messages.subject: Re: Regression with spatially autocorrelated random effects
parts:
This works better, but initialization fails when alpha is in the transformed parameters block. One key missing piece from your original model statement was that the raw values of alpha should be n(0, 1)

data {
  int n;
  int p;         //Number of x-variables
  int nPops;
  vector[n] y;
  matrix[n,p] X;
  int PopID[n];
  matrix[nPops, nPops] D;  //Distance matrix
}
parameters {
  vector[nPops] alpha_raw;
  vector[p] beta;
  real hyperMean;
  real<lower=0> lambda;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  real<lower=0> hyperSD;
}
transformed parameters{
  corr_matrix[nPops] Sigma;
  cholesky_factor_corr[nPops] L_Sigma;

  Sigma <- exp(-lambda*D);
  L_Sigma <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma);
}
model {
  vector[nPops] alpha;
  vector[n] alpha2;          // n-length alpha for vectorizing
  beta ~ normal(0, 1);       // really, beta ~ normal(0,5)
  hyperMean ~ normal(0, 1);  //mean of alpha; real sd is also 5
  lambda ~ normal(0, 1);
  alpha_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  hyperSD ~ cauchy(0, 5);
  alpha <- hyperMean 
          + (diag_pre_multiply(rep_vector(hyperSD, nPops), L_Sigma)
              * alpha_raw);  // Matt trick

  for(i in 1:n)   alpha2[i] <- alpha[PopID[i]];  
  y ~ normal(alpha2 + X*beta, sigma);
}
